name: Capacitive Nerve Induction Lance CNIL-1 'Threadneedle'
description:
The Capacitive Nerve Induction Lance is a precision energy weapon designed around a principle of extreme selectivity: rather than disrupting broad bioelectric function, it delivers a tightly focused capacitive discharge along a single projected electromagnetic filament — colloquially called 'the thread' — that is thin enough to target individual nerve trunks at range. The filament is maintained by a phased-array antenna system in the weapon's emitter head that continuously adjusts to compensate for atmospheric interference. At point of contact, the discharge induces a violent, involuntary nerve firing in the targeted structure — a single motor nerve produces a full-force muscle contraction; a sensory nerve produces an overwhelming pain signal; autonomic nerves produce effects that vary unpredictably and dangerously.

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the CNIL-1 under their 'Precision Compliance' research program, initially as a surgical adjunct for nerve stimulation procedures in patients with certain degenerative conditions. The military application was recognized almost immediately by ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS, which licensed the core technology and collaborated on the combat-ready version. The result is a weapon that demands exceptional operator training — hitting a specific nerve trunk at range requires detailed anatomical knowledge and a steady hand — but rewards that training with effects that no other platform can replicate. A shot to the brachial plexus drops a weapon instantly. A shot to the vagus nerve can stop a heart.

The weapon's cultural cachet is built on exclusivity and expertise. Threadneedle operators are known in professional circles as 'knitters' — a term that acknowledges both the weapon's filament mechanism and the surgical precision of skilled use. In assassination circles, a confirmed vagus-nerve kill is considered a mark of extraordinary craft, discussed with the kind of hushed respect usually reserved for master artisans. HELIX BIOSYSTEMS is aware of this reputation and has done nothing to discourage it.
specifications:
effective range: 25m (precision targeting), 40m (area effect, degraded)
filament diameter: ~2mm at 25m
discharge voltage: 2,200V capacitive burst (adjustable 800V–3,500V)
targeting system: Phased-array antenna with atmospheric compensation algorithm
power source: HELIX Microcapacitor Array HMC-2 (30 precision shots per array)
weight: 1.4 kg
length: 41 cm
charge cycle: 0.8 seconds between shots
operator requirement: Advanced anatomical training recommended
tactical_use: Threadneedle operators typically work from elevated positions or concealment, selecting specific nerve targets to achieve precise tactical outcomes — disarming without killing, inducing cardiac events that appear natural, or causing targeted incapacitation without leaving conventional wound evidence. In close-protection operations, skilled operators can neutralize a target in a crowd without adjacent individuals being aware anything has occurred. The weapon's limited shot count and charge cycle make it unsuitable for sustained firefights; it is a precision instrument, not a suppression tool.
cultural_context: The Threadneedle exists at the intersection of craft and violence in a way that fascinates GLMZ's professional underground. Collectors of rare weapons prize confirmed CNIL-1 units regardless of operational condition. Assassination brokers charge significant premiums for confirmed 'knitter' kills. The weapon has also developed an unlikely following among certain HELIX BIOSYSTEMS researchers who see the combat application as a perversion of their surgical tool — several have become vocal critics of the ARCTURUS licensing arrangement, with mixed results for their continued employment.
story_hooks: A senior executive died of apparent cardiac arrest during a public event. The coroner found nothing. A fixer with forensic contacts suspects vagus nerve induction but needs proof — and proof requires finding the operator.

A HELIX BIOSYSTEMS researcher has gone public about the ARCTURUS licensing deal, claiming the combat application violates the original research ethics agreement. She's received three formal warnings. Now she's missing.

A Threadneedle has appeared on the black market with its phased-array antenna modified to project multiple simultaneous filaments — an area-effect version. HELIX considers this technically impossible. Someone proved them wrong.
A known 'knitter' has retired and is teaching. Word is spreading through professional circles about where the classes are held. Multiple parties want that list of students.
ammunition_type: Helix Biosystems Compact Power Cell HB-3

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist energy rifle with an almost surgical aesthetic — longer and thinner than conventional firearms, with a pronounced emitter head that dominates the weapon's forward profile. The design reads as clinical precision rather than brutal force; it resembles specialized medical equipment more than a combat weapon. The overall silhouette is angular and refined, with sharp shoulders at the grip transition and a tapering barrel assembly.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 41 cm | Emitter head width: 6.5 cm | Grip depth: 4.2 cm | Barrel assembly length: 18 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light and balanced — 1.4 kg distributed evenly along the length creates a sensation of effortless control rather than heft. The weight sits forward of the grip, encouraging one-handed steadiness and reducing fatigue during extended positioning.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon composite frame with brushed titanium accents at stress points (grip housing, antenna mounting, trigger guard). The emitter head is polished medical-grade ceramic with embedded phased-array circuits visible as a geometric pattern beneath a translucent thermal window.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray primary body with brushed satin titanium mounting hardware. The emitter head features a subtle pearlescent shimmer from the ceramic substrate, while circuit pathways are highlighted in muted electroluminescent green that pulses faintly during standby mode.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray with titanium silver accents; muted electroluminescent green on the emitter head and around the microcapacitor array housing at the rear. Minimal branding in discrete white lettering.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with a diamond-knurl pattern, treated with a hydrophobic coating that feels slightly cool and grip-optimized for extended precision shooting. The trigger guard is wrapped in thin woven carbon fiber for sensory feedback.
distinctive_features: Phased-array antenna visible as a geometric lattice pattern within the translucent ceramic emitter head — appears as fine interlocking hexagons that glow faintly green in low light
Capacitor bank housing at the weapon's rear with illuminated charge-state indicator running along the stock: green when full, amber during cycling, red when depleted
Minimal sighting system: a narrow LED reticle projected onto a micro-display recessed into the top rail; designed for anatomical precision rather than distance estimation
Atmospheric compensation vents along the barrel assembly — small slotted apertures that release ionized air and dissipate thermal buildup

Filament discharge port at the emitter tip: a barely-visible ceramic nozzle with pinpoint precision aperture (2mm diameter) surrounded by static discharge collectors that appear as fine metallic whiskers
Serial plate mounted on the left side of the grip in minimalist white-on-gray lettering
Neural feedback loop status indicator near the thumb rest — a small display showing real-time targeting lock and nerve cluster proximity data

Wear patterns on this tier-5 example: minor scuff marks on the composite frame, slight oxidation on titanium accents suggesting field use; the emitter head shows faint scorching from repeated discharge cycles
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS mark in discrete white serif lettering on the left grip (3cm x 0.4cm) | ARCTU­RUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS licensing stamp on the rear capacitor housing | Serial number in monospace font (bottom of grip rail)
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained, well-cared-for by skilled operators. Generally shows minor cosmetic wear — small scratches on the composite, faint thermal discoloration around the emitter head from discharge cycles — but mechanical components remain pristine. Units in active service show evidence of meticulous cleaning; black market examples may show heavier wear or jury-rigged modifications to the targeting system.
